newsitem.title: USA: Busy week on tap for U.S. corp debt primary market.
newsitem.headline: Busy week on tap for U.S. corp debt primary market.

text.p: The corporate bond primary sector is in for a busy week as high-grade issuers get set to bring out an estimated $1.6 billion in the next few days, syndicate sources said.
"Several underwriters are gearing up to bring their deals to market," said one syndicate source. "We should see a lot of business in the next few days."
Leading the new issue pack is Tennessee Gas Pipeline's $800 million three-part debt offering via lead underwriter Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, sources said.
Tennessee's deal structure consist of $300 million in 20-year bonds, $200 million in 30-year debt (putable in the 10th year) and $300 million in 40-year debt, sources said.
Also getting set to come to market is Nationwide Financial's expected $400 million two-part debt offering, syndicate sources said.
The first part is expected to consist of $300 million A1/A-plus rated 30-year debt, callable after 10-years, sources said.
The second tranche is expected to consist of $100 million in A1/A rated 40-year capital securities, sources added.
